speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Duodenal Atresia. The combination of a 6-hour-old newborn with bilious vomiting, a sibling history of pyloric stenosis (suggesting a potential genetic susceptibility to GI obstructions), and the likelihood of a "double bubble" sign on the requested abdominal X-ray strongly points to duodenal atresia, often associated with Down syndrome. Please confirm if the X-ray results showed the double bubble sign and if there is any history of polyhydramnios during pregnancy.
